newsitem.title: UK: Cairn gains on planned Command buy.
newsitem.headline: Cairn gains on planned Command buy.

text.p: Cairn Energy jumped 25 pence to 397-1/2 as its planned acquisition of Australia's Command Petroleum would provide the UK oil exploration firm with the cash to develop its Sangu field off the coast of Bangladesh.
"Command is a company with cash flow and no developments, whereas Cairn is a company with developments but no cash flow," said Paul Spedding at Kleinwort Benson.
Besides any cash benefit, analyst Irene Himona at SG Strauss Turnbull also sees strategic gains coming from an acquisition of Command, which has a strong presence in India.
Himona argued that Command's Indian connections might come in useful if Cairn would want to transport gas from its Bangladeshi field into India.
"The strategic significance of this deal -- if it would go ahead -- should not be underestimated," Himona said.
Cairn earlier announced an agreed offer for Command, which would value the Australian firm at A$365 million.
Cairn plans to partly finance the acquisition through a one-for-three rights issue at 360 pence per share.
Command's main asset is its 22.5 percent interest in India's Ravva offshore oilfield.
Production from Ravva is expected to reach 35,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day by the end of 1996, which could rise to 50,000 in the longer term, Cairn said.
The British company in July set a one-for-five rights issue at 280 pence per share to raise 50.3 million stg for the development of the Sangu field, where it has made some successful test drillings.
In another move to develop Sangu, Cairn recently agreed to farm out a 25 percent interest in the field to Halliburton in exchange for its funding of 50 percent of initial costs.
